title: Father's attitude to music and the family's zither playing
summary: La Rocca says his father pushing him might have made him quit; his siblings played by notes, including zithers and tunes like La Paloma.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Do you think of anything else in your early life that may have contributed to your musical career? That is, anything else that we haven't discussed?
C-H-E-R-O-N-E-T. Well, I'll tell you what contributed more to my musical career because my daddy did want me to play and I want to play. C-H-E-R-O-N-E-T.
C-H-E-R-O-N-E-T. C-H-E-R-O-N-E-T. C-H-E-R-O-N-E-T. C-H-E-R-O-N-E-T. Because had he told me to study music, maybe I would have given it up.
That's the way I was. My mother's a music teacher.

Yeah, he told me to play the music, I would have given it up. But see, my inability to play music or to learn and nobody to teach me, yet my sisters all played. My brothers played. My older brother played violin. He played my notes. My two sisters, they played music.

No. One played a zitt and they all played by notes. They used to go around and sell these zitties with these things on. My father used to show them how to play. And at that time they used to play tunes like La Paloma. You don't hear them mention that at all. They'll tell you when the saints go marching in today. But they had numbers like Paloma over the waves mostly. I don't say all Italian music. But they were from all over. From Germany. From, I guess from every land in the world.
